Box 2 — [5172,1271,5266,1334], "logo_on_fabric", woven label patch on navy cap.
- This was the one I expected to fail. At first look the exact crop appears to clip the bottom-left border, and a 2x context crop suggested the patch ran to y~1343. It does not — that lower band is a separate bluish cap-fabric/brim highlight at y 1336-1344, a different tone from the cream border.

A column-wise scan of the bottom edge (x 5205-5258) puts the last border row at y 1327-1332, never below 1332.
- So the patch is fully contained. Margins: left 3px, top 3px, right 4px, bottom 2px.

- mark_type correct: embroidered manufacturer label on fabric, not a vehicle plate.

1. The bottom margins are tighter than the sweep claimed. Box 2's confirmation says "~3 px (3-5%) of cap fabric around it" on every side; the real bottom margin is 2px. Box 1's bottom margin is 1-2px at the faintest antialiased fringe. If the masking step erodes or feathers inward, a 1px halo of the mark's soft edge could survive at the bottom of either box. Dilating both boxes by 2-3px before masking would be cheap insurance; the surrounding pixels are plain white panel and plain navy fabric, so there is nothing good to destroy.
2. I independently checked the two judgement calls the sweep flagged, and agree with both. The dryer smudge at x 2028-2061, y 2054-2085 resolves under contrast stretch into two small dark blobs with no circular emblem and no letterforms — not legible as any brand mark, correctly left unboxed. The cap patch that the sweep self-reported as undeclared is real and is the box 2 mark. Separately, I noticed illegible dark markings further right on the washer panel around x 1280-1340, y 2330-2400; stretched to 7x they read as control-panel labelling/texture, not a wordmark, so no box is warranted there either.

audit.verdict:
Audited all 24 boxes across the 4 images by cropping each pixel_box exactly at full resolution and viewing it, plus contrast-stretched and high-pass relief views with coordinate grids over box-plus-margin, and threshold / connected-component measurements wherever a call was tight. 21 boxes are good; 3 are genuinely defective.

Geometry and metadata all check out. All four files really are 4000x6000 (verified with sips). Every one of the 24 normalised boxes recomputes exactly from its pixel_box against those real dimensions - maximum deviation across all 96 coordinates is 0.000000. No mark_type errors: there are no vehicle plates anywhere in this set (all four images are gym interiors), nothing is mislabelled as number_plate or should be, and "text_line" for the moulded ROGUE wordmarks vs "logo_on_fabric" for the shoe/shirt/sock marks is applied correctly throughout.

The three defects, in order of severity:
1. row_poster.jpg [2160,4710,2218,4764] - a false positive. The crop holds two tiny specular highlights on a seam, not a UA logo. This is the destroys-good-pixels failure mode; recommend dropping the box entirely.
2. frontsquat_poster.jpg [126,2502,478,2800] - final E of ROGUE clipped by ~5px on the right (letter measured to x482, box ends at 478).
3. bench_poster_alt.jpg [0,1330,66,1470] - the frame-clipped E's lowest arm clipped by ~13px at the bottom and its spine by ~4px on the right.

Findings 2 and 3 are small in absolute terms but are measured and reproducible, not eyeballed; each would leave a thin residual sliver of a trademark letter adjacent to the inpainted patch. If your masking pipeline dilates by 8px or more before filling, both are absorbed automatically and only finding 1 needs action.

The other 21 boxes were verified as containing their described mark completely, with sensible margins and none excessively large. Notably tight-but-correct cases I measured rather than assumed: bench_poster_alt [2826,1812,3158,2134] (far-plate ROGUE, E clears the bottom-right corner by ~20px) and frontsquat_poster_alt [3240,2344,3656,2556] (mirrored R's strokes end at x~3630, 26px clear of the 3656 edge - the isolated structure at x3652-3660 is the plate rim arc, not the letter). The two bench_poster_alt footwear side-stripe boxes are accurate: the near shoe's tail genuinely runs down to y~5410 where it meets the midsole, matching the 5412 bottom edge, and the second shoe's device is correctly clipped at the x=4000 frame edge. The frontsquat_poster chest X measures x2377-2458/y3198-3262 inside its [2374,3194,2462,3266] box at every threshold from 60 to 150.

Three non-defect observations worth passing on, none of which affect masking: the bench_poster_alt [3188,4926,3258,4996] patch sits at the lace/collar top rather than strictly on the tongue as described, but the box is correct; the frontsquat_poster shoe-toe device is on the frame-left shoe, which is the athlete's right foot, so the "athlete's left training shoe" wording is inverted while the box is right; and I independently checked the far shoe's collar in row_poster (~2415-2470/4505-4555), which at full magnification resolves as bright floor seen past the collar edge plus a lace-loop highlight rather than a UA, so that file's "not_found" note is defensible.

audit.verdict:
CLEAN - no bad boxes found. I audited 35 boxes on slabvault_results_reference.png (1512x2268, dimensions confirmed) by cropping each pixel_box at full resolution, viewing it, and independently re-deriving the mark's extent numerically.

METHOD AND RESULTS
1) Caption line 1 (12 boxes) and caption line 2 (6 boxes): for each I took a padded window, thresholded at luminance<200, grouped contiguous ink rows into text-line bands, and compared each band to the box. Every box's ink band is exactly [x0..x1-1] x [y0..y1-1] - no glyph body outside, nothing excessive. Descender claims check out: #2/#4/#11 ('pp' in Upper/Topps), #3 ('y' in Blue-Eyes), #6 ('pp','y' + the period of 'Jr.'), #7 ('g' x2 in Magic/Gathering), #8/#9/#12 ('y'/'J') are all 18px-tall boxes that contain the descenders; the three 15px boxes (#1, #5, #10) are on strings with no descenders, correctly shorter. I read every crop and the text matches the `what` field in all 18 cases. The six tiles with no line-2 box have "#23"/"#221"/"#1"/"#53"/"#138"/"#1" there - correctly omitted, not missed marks.
2) Holder-label blocks (12 boxes): the earlier luminance<190 measurement is contaminated by the slab's plastic edge (x~131/~1210), so I re-profiled at luminance<140 with per-band column-run splitting. All 12 boxes contain their three printed lines in full; the apparent "text outside the box" on tiles 7 and 8 is the large grade digit ('8' at x 999-1006; '9' at x 1358-1363), separated by a wide gap and correctly excluded, as is the red label border in every case. Tile 6's label really does sit ~3-4px higher than its neighbours (text rows 962-968 / 972-978 / 983-989), so box #24's y0=962 is right, not a mistake. Label contents match the `what` strings exactly on all 12.
3) Card faces (5 boxes): I read the edge transitions rather than trusting the notes. Tiles 1/2/3 (dark cards on light plastic) transition at exactly x0 and x1-1, y0 and y1-1 on luminance scanlines. Tile 4 (white-bordered LeBron card) confirmed on the plastic~185-213 -> card-white 227+ step: card spans 1224-1369 x 439-641, matching the box exactly. Tile 5 (yellow Pikachu card) confirmed on a saturation profile (bg 3-20, card 60-150): card spans 144-289 x 1024-1227, matching. No plastic included, no card edge cut off.
4) Normalised vs pixel: recomputed all 35 against 1512x2268. Every one agrees; the only differences are last-digit rounding (e.g. #5 0.166 vs 0.16601, #19 0.18033 vs 0.18034).
5) mark_type: appropriate throughout. There is no vehicle, licence plate or number plate anywhere in this asset set, so nothing is mislabelled as or away from number_plate. Using "other" for the whole copyrighted card face is the right call; the 12 label blocks are tagged text_line although each spans three printed lines - a naming nit, not a geometry problem.

ONE ADVISORY (not a bad box, applies to all text boxes uniformly)
Every text box is the exact ink bbox with ZERO margin, not the "~1px of blank page around it" the confirmations claim. A faint antialias fringe (luminance ~210-228 against a ~233-240 background) sits immediately outside many of them - e.g. row 748 above box #1, x=211 right of box #19, x=221 right of #27, row 1580 below #29, row 989 below #24. Masking on these coordinates literally will leave a faint 1px ghost outline of each wordmark. Dilate every text_line box by 1-2px before masking. I did not list these as bad boxes because no glyph body falls outside any box and flagging 30 boxes for a subpixel halo would be manufacturing findings.

SCOPE LIMIT
The boxes JSON I was handed is truncated mid-sentence inside the 35th entry ("Card face, tile 5 ... saturation profile (4-14 on p"). Card faces for tiles 6-12 were presumably in the cut-off remainder and were NOT audited - 35 is everything I actually received. Separately, I checked the other 14 JPGs in the folder: they contain only invented brands and people (GRADEX, APEX, SlabVault Cards, Ironclad, Warp Rider, Nightglass, Solaris, "Dale Corriveau", "Andre Bishop", etc.), no real trademarks, so the payload's single-image scope looks correct rather than incomplete.

audit.verdict:
Audited all 24 boxes by cropping each pixel_box at full resolution and viewing it, plus threshold-based ink-extent measurement (luminance local-contrast for the dark-cloth spines and the painted signs, R-B "warmth" for gilt on dark cloth, dark-on-light polarity for the tan spine). 4 of 24 boxes are bad; all 4 are under-sized (clipping), none is over-sized.

CONFIRMED BAD (4): (1) books "THE SEA" - clips the T/H foot serifs by ~10px at the bottom and the A apex by ~4px at the top; (2) books "OF WILD FLOWERS" - the left edge bisects the 'O' of OF, leaving ~5-7px of the letter outside; (3) bookshop "for curious minds" - the top edge cuts ~22px off the 'd' ascender of "minds"; (4) bookshop "Coastal Books" - the top edge cuts ~7px off the 'k' ascender of "Books".

CHECKS THAT PASSED: Image dimensions - all three declared image_size values match the files exactly (3000x3000, 3800x2533, 3400x2267). Normalised coordinates - every one of the 24 normalised boxes recomputes from its pixel_box to within 1e-6 (pure rounding); no pixel/normalised disagreement anywhere. mark_type - all 24 are "text_line", which is correct: these are a book stack, a cider-barn interior and a bookshop interior, with no vehicle anywhere in frame, so nothing is a mis-labelled number_plate and nothing labelled otherwise is one.

CLEAN BOXES: all 5 cider-barn sign boxes (RIVERDALE, CIDER, TRADITIONAL CIDER, SMALL BATCH, LOCAL APPLES) fully contain their lines with 4-11px margins - the final 'E' of RIVERDALE ends at x~448 inside the 452 edge, and the final 'R' of CIDER at x~372/y~592 inside 377/597. In the books image, all five COLLINS wordmarks, all five spine titles other than THE SEA, all five author credits, and the cover line "THE OBSERVER'S BOOK" are contained. Two false alarms I chased and cleared: the ink 12px left of the red-spine COLLINS box is the blind-stamped scallop motif, not the wordmark; and the ink below the "THE OBSERVER'S BOOK" box is line 2's own letters, not that line's descenders.

TIGHT BUT NOT REPORTED (contained, zero-to-small slack - worth knowing before feathering a mask): books "THE NATURAL WORLD" right edge sits exactly on the final D's edge (both 1462, 0px margin); the 'J' of "J. ARTHUR THOMSON" reaches y=2219 against a 2218 bottom (1px); the 'H' of "H. E. BATES" bottoms out within ~1px of its 1250 edge.

PROCESS NOTE: the per-box "confirmed" strings are not trustworthy as evidence. Several state glyph extents that disagree with the pixels - e.g. the OF box claims the O spans x=895-928 when it spans ~888-916, and the THE SEA box cites "T stem bottom y=1292" while the T's foot serif actually reaches ~1305. Every one of the four defects is in a box whose note asserted the mark was "fully inside with ~3px margin", so those notes should not be relied on in place of re-checking.
